newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Lodz sells first municipal bond tranche.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Lodz sells first municipal bond tranche.

text.p: A consortium of banks managing a 29 million zloty municipal bond issue for the central Polish city of Lodz sold the first tranche of seven million zlotys to nine domestic non-banking institutions, Lodz's president said.
Marek Czekalski said the next tranches of the issue, directed to selected investors and worth 13 and nine million zlotys would be launched on October 4 and November 8 respectively.
"Lodz's strategy is to attract investors and this (the bond issue) proved to be a good way to do it - the first tranche was a success," he told a news conference on Friday.
He added that the issue, managed by the Polish branch of Internationale Nederlanden Groep, Bank Slaski and Bank Przemyslowy SA w Lodzi, would finance the modernisation of Lodz's transport system.

The bonds have maturities of one, two, three and four years and carry coupons of 0.35, 0.65, 0.9, 1.15 percentage points above the average yield of 52-week treasury bills, last sold at 19.42 percent. The nominal value of the bonds is 100 zlotys.
Czekalski said Lodz was considering another bond issue in the next two years. He did not rule out a public issue or a eurobond issue.
"If this issue proves to be a success, we will try to attract capital through more bond issues," he said.
